anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Statistics on tables and indexes are stale, incomplete, or missing, causing systematic cardinality mis-estimation.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly: The optimizer chooses an execution plan that is sub-optimal despite reasonably accurate statistics because of cost-model or plan-cache issues.
CPU Resource Anomaly: Database processes oversubscribe CPU cores, driving sustained CPU saturation and run-queue contention.

When these three root causes coexist, the workload experiences volatile and often catastrophic performance swings: grossly inaccurate cardinality estimates feed the cost model, which in turn selects poor or erratic plans that consume excessive CPU. The resulting CPU saturation starves concurrent sessions, inflates run-queue and context-switch waits, and lengthens response times across the system. Rapid back-to-back hard parses may cache alternating bad plans, so successive executions of the same statement oscillate between different, CPU-hungry strategies (e.g., serial full scans versus massively parallel nested loops). Because CPUs are already pegged, even small misestimations translate into severe slowdowns, and the statistical discrepancies become harder to detect—the usual tell-tale gaps between estimated and actual rows are obscured by global resource queuing. End-users observe unpredictable latencies, timeouts, and throughput collapse, while DBAs see both plan-quality warnings and system-level CPU alarms firing simultaneously.

Causally, stale or poor-quality statistics misguide costing; the optimizer, already susceptible to plan-selection pitfalls (e.g., parameter-sensitive reuse, version changes, missing hints), is more likely to lock in an inefficient plan. That plan inflates CPU demand—via unnecessary scans, mismatched join methods, or excessive parallelism—driving the host into sustained CPU saturation. High CPU pressure, in turn, expands parse times and reduces the effectiveness of adaptive mechanisms, delaying automatic statistics refresh jobs and making it harder for the optimizer to re-evaluate plans, thus reinforcing the feedback loop. The intertwined effects of bad statistics, wrong plan choices, and compute exhaustion therefore amplify each other, producing a severe composite anomaly that degrades both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it.
entry.trigger_condition: An interactive session remains idle longer than interactive_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the idle interactive connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
